newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin court convicts Stasi officers for RAF aid.
newsitem.headline: Berlin court convicts Stasi officers for RAF aid.

text.p: A Berlin court on Friday found three East German Stasi intelligence officers guilty of helping wanted Red Army Faction (RAF) guerrillas escape justice in West Germany and sentenced them to two years' probation.
The court also issued formal reprimands to the three Stasi officers and said they would be fined between 2,400 marks ($1,400) and 5,000 marks ($2,900) if they violate the terms of their probation.

The former Stasi officers were charged with helping the RAF guerrillas escape justice by providing them with new identities and cover in communist East Germany. The guerrillas were regarded as some of West Germany's most dangerous criminals.

Susanne Albrecht had been wanted for her part in the 1977 murder of banker Juergen Ponto, the chairman of Dresdner Bank in Frankfurt. Silke Maier-Witt and Monika Helbing were wanted in connection with the 1977 kidnapping and murder of Employers' Federation chief Hanns-Martin Schleyer and other RAF attacks.

The guerrillas were taken in on orders from former Stasi chief Erich Mielke and witnesses have testified that Honecker had known of the operation. The arrests of the 10 guerrillas in summer 1990 shocked Germans on both sides of the Cold War divide.
Defence lawyers in the case argued their clients do not dispute they helped to give the retired guerrillas a new start in life, but deny perverting the course of justice.
